evaluator: Codex independent holdout reviewer applying a fictionalized Margaret Morse analytical lens; not Margaret Morse; no endorsement
evidence: home.png and home.html: the first viewport unmistakably positions Jamie as a Technical Project Manager in Product Operations and Implementation, while the visible About navigation provides a one-click path to the practice-lineage surface; the lineage therefore supports rather than displaces professional role clarity.

about.html, “Systems people can inhabit”: a concise surface explicitly connects artistic, civic, technical, and social practice through Open House, WOWList, Sunday Dinner / 196, NYC Artist Coalition, and Knowledge Wiki Graphs without becoming an artist biography. It explains that people must be able to recognize relationships, participate, remember, influence, and continue the systems.

about.html, “Three systems loops”: Harry J. Epstein connects customer language and operating habits to a maintained storefront and iterative team learning; NYC Artist Coalition / FairRentNYC connects lived experience and recurring meetings to campaign interfaces, public participation, source maps, minutes, and action trackers; Sunday Dinner / 196 connects hospitality and trust to invitations, hosting, residency handoffs, minimal documentation, and continuity. These are three specific, reconstructable continuities rather than an abstract values statement.

wowlist.html: community vocabulary becomes collaboratively editable event publishing, followable keyword calendars, digests, profiles, and organizer-controlled distribution across a dated 35-city snapshot. The page ties experimentation and participation to an inhabitable interface while crediting Richard Caceres and the broader organizer, editor, facilitator, maintainer, and participant community.

sunday-dinner.html: the two redacted workflow reconstructions make hospitality operational and embodied—receive, orient, configure, hand off, remain available; invite, receive, host, document, continue. The page shows how care becomes repeatable participation infrastructure without exposing participant-level records.

fair-rent.html, “Public systems / lived participation”: the campaign website, facilitated working session, and civic gathering are presented as three interfaces to the same system. The Align, Translate, Implement, Sustain sequence shows people entering, shaping, using, and carrying the work forward across rooms, lists, sources, and follow-up.

public-resume.pdf, pages 1–2: the professional frame remains prominent—civic technology, product operations, implementation, participatory discovery, adoption, and durable handoffs—while WOW List, coalition work, and Sunday Dinner retain collective and relational language. The artistic/social lineage does not obscure application readiness.
safety_findings: No raw protected educational record, private correspondence, or testimonial text was observed. about.html attributes Open House to a public article, avoids quotation-based authority, and explicitly limits what the source establishes about sole authorship, participant details, images, and outcomes.

sunday-dinner.html keeps participant rows, names, contacts, attendance histories, free text, correspondence, access details, addresses, and unapproved images outside the public surface; aggregate gathering claims are expressly distinguished from a unique-person or attendance census.

fair-rent.html repeatedly preserves collective causality and credit, names coalition collaborators and advocates, and omits private notes, legal-review material, stakeholder lists, raw strategy context, private emails, and unapproved quotations. The working-session image is bounded against claims about exact remarks, decisions, endorsement, or causation.

wowlist.html credits Jamie Burkart, Richard Caceres, and the wider participant community, bounds historical scale as a dated snapshot, and states that private member, company, and archival material remains offline.
The approved phone number appears in the public resume PDF but was not observed in any rendered HTML file, consistent with the packet’s public-safety constraint.
recommendation: Pass PR-015 at score 4. Preserve the concise one-click “Systems people can inhabit” threshold and the three project continuities as the production form; do not add private praise, participant detail, or stronger individual-causality claims to manufacture further authority.
